headline: Funding surges. Space traffic intensifies. Budgets expand.
deck: This week saw a flurry of funding and strategic partnerships as the space industry gears up for a more crowded orbital environment.

stories.head: Impulse Space raises $500 million for orbital Ubers
stories.body: Impulse Space has secured $500 million to accelerate production of its orbital transfer vehicles. This investment highlights the increasing demand for in-space transportation, as companies look to facilitate satellite deployments and other missions. With this cash infusion, Impulse is positioning itself as a key player in the growing market for space logistics.
stories.soWhat: The race for in-space transport is heating up, and those not in the driver’s seat might find themselves left behind in the orbital traffic jam.

stories.head: Voyager acquires Astrobotic for lunar ambitions
stories.body: Voyager Technologies is set to acquire lunar lander developer Astrobotic for up to $300 million. This move underscores the ongoing interest in lunar exploration and the commercial opportunities surrounding it. Astrobotic’s expertise in lunar landings could bolster Voyager's portfolio as it aims to capitalize on the moon's potential resources.
stories.soWhat: As lunar real estate heats up, expect more acquisitions as companies scramble to stake their claims before the land rush really begins.

stories.head: USFY27 budget adds $1.4B for space resilience
stories.body: The recent FY27 budget markup includes an additional $1.4 billion allocated for space resilience initiatives. This increase signals a recognition of the growing threats to satellite operations and the need for enhanced protective measures. The funding aims to bolster capabilities in space traffic management and satellite safety.
stories.soWhat: With more money flowing into space resilience, the real challenge will be translating dollars into effective strategies that prevent orbital collisions.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's Series C
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's recent $190 million funding round could indicate a shift towards co-orbital security solutions, which are becoming increasingly critical.

watchlist.title: Watch for Anduril and L3Harris partnership outcomes
watchlist.body: Their collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid could reshape the competitive landscape in space surveillance and defense.

watchlist.title: Impacts of GPS jamming on commercial operations
watchlist.body: With GPS jamming returning to pre-2024 levels, insurers and operators will need to reassess risks and operational strategies in affected regions.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program may signal a longer-term commitment to data-driven defense solutions.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
